newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Telkom to set up multimedia venture. [CORRECTED 03:31 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Telkom to set up multimedia venture. [CORRECTED 03:31 GMT]

text.p: Indonesian telecommunications giant PT Telkom said on Monday it had signed a joint venture aggreement with three companies linked to conglomerate Bimantara Citra to provide interactive multimedia services.
It said the joint venture, named PT Telemedia Indonesia, will have an equity of 10 billion rupiah and paid up capital of 2.5 billion rupiah.

"The joint venture agreement was signed on October 22 (corrects the date from October 2) with PT Telkom controlling a 35 percent stake, PT Asriland holding 25 percent, PT Telekomindo Prima Bhakti and PT Rajawali Citra Televisi Indonesia holding 20 percent each," the statement said.
Rajawali is a unit of Bimantara, a conglomerate controlled by President Suharto's second son, Bambang Trihatmodjo. Telekomindo is a cellular phone venture co-owned by Telkom and Rajawali.
Asriland, wholly owned by Trihatmodjo, owns 38.41 percent of Bimantara.
